items.issue: The earlier registry wording '150-400 m positional offsets' overstates the official Hermant et al. (2025) PDF. Figure 2 supports that a local distance between USGS Quaternary traces and TLS fault labels can be up to 400 m; it does not establish a general 150-400 m distribution, a 150 m lower bound, or the H27-10 100-300 m annulus. Separately, the local 0.2477 raster has 5,355 dots at d_cat=100 m and 8,769 at d_cat<=200 m; on B_oof (seeds 130-139) the d_cat=100 m removed band has efficiency 0.0034 vs the live 0.0521 break-even.
items.action: Correct the source wording; retain H27-4's measured 100 m prune result, but do not infer that the adjacent H27-10 annulus is productive. Do not cite failed habitat tomography as evidence. Addendum F later tested the narrowed H27-10 reallocation on seeds 150-159 and its frozen gate failed; current result and same-seed integrity-recheck disclosure are in knowledge/07_untried_hypotheses.md and the h27-10-first-run-spacing-diagnostic-self-distance item.

items.issue: knowledge/01 and the operating-point model assume |G| ~ 12.63k px. items.issue: A habitat tomography of the hidden truth (20 live scores as 20 linear measurements of the truth intensity lambda) is NOT identifiable from the available corpus. Overlapping bases: in-sample R2 = -1.24. Strict 7-cell catalogue-distance partition: R2 = -0.360, leave-one-submission-out score RMSE 0.0715 vs a score spread of 0.0686 (signal ratio 0.96).
items.action: Recorded so no future session re-derives it or - worse - ships an emission chosen by the fitted lambda. The fitted habitat weights (66% of truth in the 100-200 m catalogue ring) are hypothesis-generating ONLY. evidence/live_truth_partition_radial.json.

items.issue: The live-validated retention rule credit(d) = credit_solid * c(d)/c_solid assumes the hidden truth is spread uniformly near the emission. That is exactly right for geometric (Poisson-disk) thinning - it predicts two independent live solid->dotted pairs to -0.1% and +4.0% - but it is biased against TARGETED pruning, because it charges every removed pixel with average credit. The out-of-fold gate measured the H27-4 catalogue-flank pixels directly at 0.0034 credit/px, about 15x below the 0.0521 live break-even.
items.action: Report BOTH models for every candidate (evidence/candidate_model_scores.json): 'geometric' charges uniform-truth retention for all changes, 'hybrid' charges geometric retention for thinning and the measured OOF efficiencies for the targeted steps. Slot 1 vs slot 3 is the live A/B that settles which is right. Neither column is a score.

items.issue: CI was RED on `main` before Session 3 and nobody had noticed. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `python -m pytest -q` on a bare checkout, but `data_cache/` is git-ignored by design and CI cannot restore it (`scripts/restore_data.py` reads the inputs from SIBLING repositories, which the workflow's `contents: read` GITHUB_TOKEN cannot access). `tests/test_vector_and_oof.py::test_vector_attribution_and_evidence_files` opens `paths.TEMPLATE`, so it failed with `RasterioIOError: data_cache/sample_submission.tif: No such file or directory`. Reproduced on the base commit `ce80ead` in a clean clone: 1 failed, 35 passed.
items.action: Fixed in Session 3 with `tests/conftest.py`: a `requires_rasters` marker plus a collection hook that skips with the missing file names in the reason. Applied to the pre-existing test and to the new `test_verify_downloads_still_passes_with_four_slots`. Verified in a clean clone without `data_cache`: 45 passed, 2 skipped; and locally after `restore_data.py`: 47 passed, 0 skipped. A red suite now always means a real failure. Consequence to record honestly: **CI does not exercise the two raster-dependent checks** - they run locally and must be re-run before any release. Adding a data-restore step to CI needs a token with read access to the sibling repositories, which is an access request for the owner, not something the agent can grant itself.

items.issue: Every gate this programme has run hides pieces of the CATALOGUE, so 100% of hidden truth (120,983 px over the Addendum-D cells) lies at distance 0 from the published catalogue and Habitat A (>=300 m away) contains NO truth by construction. The live-scored 0.2477 emission puts 81.4% of its dots >=300 m from the catalogue (median 1.5 km). The proxy is therefore blind to the habitat that carries the real credit - the standing caveat 'catalogue-internal truth overstates real-world enrichment', now with numbers.

(2) The question is registered as a bounded live measurement instead - Addendum E, Slot 5 (gems27-...-a34b0799df59), which changes only WHICH far-field pixels are emitted at fixed pixel count. evidence/arm_habitat_decomposition.json.

items.issue: data_cache/prepared/features.npy band 'det_local_relief' is SIGNED (min -207.686, max +299.416, mean -0.026, 64.7% negative) and carries 3,061 NaN; the lidar_* columns carry 24.63% NaN (the LiDAR-invalid footprint), not 0. items.issue: The second-moment quantity sum(l^2)/area is the standard continuous connectivity measure for 2-D line networks, but no critical value for it could be verified from an official source inside this sandbox (only github.com and pypi.org are reachable; the Berkowitz et al. 2000 text available here gives the P criterion, not a sum(l^2) threshold).
items.action: sum(l^2) = 56,580 km^2 (1.095 per unit area) is reported as a continuous RELATIVE measure and as the tie-break inside equal |dP| only. No pass/fail claim anywhere in the repo rests on it. The paper-verified threshold statement remains P = 5.784 -> 6.124 against Pc = 5.6-6.0.

items.issue: Before any Euler model fit, the local input audit found no unit metadata in the owner-mirror magnetic band tags and no explicit magnetic-source-depth band. Protocol revision 2 (commit 524bf27) corrected the unit wording before any fit; Euler positions/depths are invariant to a constant unit conversion, but physical units remain unauthenticated. items.issue: Session 4 measured that the standing spatially-blocked holdout hides catalogue components INTERLEAVED with the known catalogue, so 100% of its hidden truth sits at distance 0 from the full published catalogue (evidence/arm_habitat_decomposition.json: habitat_A truth = 0 px of 120,983). Because scripts/verify_downloads.py requires zero pixels on catalogue cells, a shippable file can only occupy habitat A. The harness therefore cannot validate any ADDITION arm - and Session 10's reachability frontier shows the gap to the public leaderboard #1 (+1,151 px credit at the current budget, 24.0% more credit than we capture) is closable only by addition arms. Every prior gate result is a pruning result.
items.action: Session 10 added src/gems27/losfo.py (leave-fault-system-out: whole fault systems held out with a 600 m label buffer erased, so truth is >= 600 m from every pixel the detector saw as positive) and scripts/run_losfo_harness.py, which scores the SAME held-out systems under a masked-label detector and an unmasked control to quantify the catalogue-interpolation inflation. tests/test_losfo.py guards the no-leakage invariant, including a scipy binary_dilation(iterations=0) trap that returns an all-True array and would have silently merged every fault into one system. Evidence: evidence/losfo_farfield_diagnostic.json. This is a measurement instrument, not a promotion gate.

items.issue: The merge-triggered runner run at 2026-10-03T18:49:01Z (commit acc4c09) DID download and pin-verify the H33-1 slip/dilation-tendency release correctly (http 200, 35,912,323 bytes, sha256 5d6213f7... pin_match true, status DERIVED_WRITTEN) but committed docs/data/sb_slip_tendency_in_footprint.{csv,json} with n_records = 0. Root cause: ScienceBase download URLs carry no file suffix (.../catalog/file/get/<item>?f=__disk__33%2Fb0%2F91%2F...), so fetch() named the payload sb_slip_tendency_shapefile_full.bin; the derived step then treated .bin as a direct vector layer instead of an archive and GDAL reported DataSourceError 'not recognized as being in a supported file format'. The failure was recorded per-layer as LAYER_UNREADABLE rather than hidden, but the overall row still said DERIVED_WRITTEN, so an empty table looked like success and the job exited 0. SECOND DEFECT FOUND 2026-10-03T18:54:08Z: after the magic-byte fix the archive opened correctly (payload_format zip, payload_used sb_slip_tendency_shapefile_full.zip) and the real layer was found - GB_Quaternary_faults_TD_TS.shp, whose name indicates dilation tendency (TD) and slip tendency (TS) attributes - but the read failed with 'ImportError: geopandas is required to use pyogrio.read_dataframe()'. The workflow installed pyogrio shapely pyproj pandas but not geopandas. The job exited non-zero (the new fail-loudly guard worked as intended) and sciencebase_derived_written = 0.
items.action: Fixed the same session. scripts/fetch_external_layers.py gained resolve_payload_format(), which decides the format from MAGIC BYTES first (PK\x03\x04 -> zip), then the pinned filename, and copies the payload to a correctly-suffixed name without mutating the hashed original. build_sciencebase_derived now reports LAYER_UNREADABLE / DERIVED_EMPTY / NO_VECTOR_LAYER / ARCHIVE_UNREADABLE as distinct non-success statuses, and fetch-gdr-external-layers.yml fails the job on any of them plus PIN_MISMATCH, so an unusable clip can no longer be committed silently. Regression tests: test_payload_without_a_zip_suffix_is_still_recognised_as_a_zip, test_derived_run_on_a_dot_bin_payload_produces_records, test_unreadable_layer_is_not_reported_as_written. The currently committed docs/data/sb_slip_tendency_in_footprint.{csv,json} are EMPTY and must not be used as the H33-1 data precondition; the next merge re-triggers the bridge. SECOND FIX (same session): the workflow now installs geopandas and runs an explicit import-assert step naming pyogrio/shapely/pyproj/pandas/geopandas before fetching; test_runner_installs_geopandas_for_read_dataframe and test_workflow_fails_the_job_on_every_unusable_clip_status guard both. H33-1's data precondition remains UNSATISFIED until a run reports DERIVED_WRITTEN with n_records > 0 and a schema listing slip/dilation-tendency fields. Note the layer name GB_Quaternary_faults_TD_TS.shp is evidence toward that schema but is not yet proof of the field names.
